base: vm_malbolge/src/min3_echo1.hell (verified echo artifact) + new stack_scratch/stack_top cells
test: store input byte in DEDICATED cells, recover it, emit; compares against identity

attempts.variant: single-level store: crazy(byte, stack_top=C1); recover 2x crazy(C2)
attempts.result: FAIL (deterministic): 00->54, 41->67, 7a->dd, ff->55 on oracle AND runner (self-consistent, wrong value)
attempts.conclusion: crazy writes result to BOTH cell and A. The proven echo idiom stores through TWO levels (tmp1 sacrificial then tmp2); 2x C2-crazy recovery inverts exactly that two-level chain. Preserved as evidence of the ternary semantics.

attempts.variant: two-level store: crazy A into stack_scratch (C1), then crazy A into stack_top (C1); recover 2x crazy(C2, stack_top)

verdict: A dedicated cell pair (stack_scratch + stack_top), created by this experiment (not the example's tmp1..tmp4), stores one input byte and returns it intact. Pattern: ENTRY double-crazy inits both cells to C1; store = crazy A->stack_scratch then crazy A->stack_top; recover = ROT C2 + crazy stack_top, twice. Cost ~4327 steps over plain echo (26020 vs 21693).
scope_limits: One-bit-deep stack: exactly two paired cells, single value; no push/pop of multiple values.
Round trip happens inside an otherwise-sequential program; NOT integrated into opcode dispatch, no second fetch, no loop.
store->recover distance is short (no intervening dispatches); persistence under interleaved dispatch operations NOT demonstrated.
